statement: A systems-level gap may exist between current AI-native protocols and verified mission outcomes.
notes: Deterministic work supports a systems integration problem, but STEAD overlap narrows novelty and STUDY-011 does not validate the old D1/D2/D3 gate narrative. Treat the gap as scoped and contestable, not a settled new-discipline claim.

statement: Evidence-gated completion can reduce false completion in long-horizon agent tasks.
notes: MISSION-Bench supports the mechanism in deterministic/simulated workloads. In preregistered STUDY-011, H1 was REVERSED because baseline A abstained enough to floor FCR at 0; do not claim live confirmation of the old FCR hypothesis.

statement: A vendor-neutral mission contract can improve cross-runtime portability.
notes: Supported across in-tree Native/LangGraph/AutoGen/Node-style validation surfaces. Independent external reproduction remains pending, so this is not an external replication claim.

statement: Human-first mission UX can outperform chat-only interaction on verified outcome efficiency.
notes: N=0 live humans. The 6.6→2.0 HEVO result is a deterministic GOMS/persona simulation used to validate the measurement pipeline, not evidence of human preference or efficiency.

statement: Control and verification overhead can be economically justified by improved verified outcomes.
notes: The reported CPVO improvement is supported inside the deterministic/simulated benchmark cost model. Live billed-cost evidence and sensitivity analysis are still required for a general economic claim.

statement: AIE should remain separate from ISE while potentially contributing authority semantics.
source_refs: research program architecture and decision records
notes: Program boundary decision; not an empirical efficacy claim.

statement: Tool invocation and resource reading are solved by Model Context Protocol (MCP).
notes: Reuse MCP transport/tool semantics; do not reinvent tool transport. 'Solved' is scoped to the transport/interface role, not every security or governance concern.

statement: LLM application telemetry is converging on OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions.
notes: Reuse OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry primitives where they fit; convergence does not make telemetry an authority source.

statement: Workload identity is addressed by SPIFFE/SPIRE while dynamic mission delegation still requires separate authority semantics.
notes: SPIFFE/SPIRE addresses workload identity. The stronger claim that delegation authority is broadly unsolved must remain scoped against current external work; Muse is architectural convergence, not validation of Aftergraph semantics.

statement: Agent self-reported completion exhibits material false-completion risk in evaluated long-horizon workloads.
notes: Retain the observed failure mode, but do not promote one 15–45% or 84.7% range to a population-level universal rate. Rates depend on workload, verifier and failure injection.

statement: Progressive disclosure can reduce contract-comprehension degradation in smaller-model simulations.
notes: Q3-2026 tier parameters are calibrated estimates, not live measurements of named <=14B models. Live confirmation remains pending.

statement: Monolithic new standards may face higher adoption friction than compositional profiles.
notes: Use as a design/standardization hypothesis, not a measured adoption law.

statement: A three-tier progressive disclosure contract can keep the core schema footprint under 250 tokens in the measured implementation.
notes: Measured core payload footprint was 227 tokens in the referenced implementation; third-party tool definitions add separate context cost.

statement: Deterministic JSON serialization enables tamper-evident signing inputs for mission contracts and delegation grants.
notes: This supports deterministic signing inputs; it does not by itself prove key custody, signer identity or distributed non-repudiation.

statement: Reference Runtime v0.1 intercepts agent self-reported completion and deterministically enforces the implemented completion/evidence invariants.
notes: Implementation claim only. External architectural convergence such as Muse does not validate SPEC-001 or AIE conformance.

statement: Closed-loop automated diagnostic recovery reduced Cost Per Verified Outcome by 81.3% in MISSION-Bench's tested cost model.
notes: The 81.3% figure is specific to the deterministic/simulated benchmark cost and failure distribution. It is not a general live-provider economics result.

statement: Purpose-bound authority attenuation blocked unauthorized capability executions in the evaluated deterministic/adversarial fixtures.
notes: 0 observed unauthorized actions in evaluated fixtures is not a population-level security guarantee. STUDY-011 H2 supports a marginal authority+budget effect over assurance in both live provider strata, not universal zero-UAR.

statement: An in-tree independently authored runtime implementation passes the program's cross-domain SPEC-001 validation suite.
notes: The alternate implementation is independently authored within the same program/repository lineage. Do not describe it as blind external reproduction; that maturity gate remains pending.
